title: Long Hearts with top control
author_notes: Reviewed during EC-033 implementation; see docs/COACHING_REVIEW.md. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: Four may be too cautious
feedback.summary: Four top Hearts plus two side Aces create overtrick pressure. A low target is not automatically safer.
points: Control: Ace-King-Queen-Jack of Hearts lead a six-card trump holding.
Probable: the Spade and Diamond Aces offer side tricks if opponents follow suit.
Risk: long opposing trump or side-suit ruffs can change the total; too low a bid also creates overtrick pressure.

feedback.title: A controlled Heart plan
feedback.summary: Five Hearts balances a strong trump sequence with useful side controls, while allowing for imperfect side winners.

feedback.title: Six has support and conditions
feedback.summary: Six Hearts is plausible from trump control and side Aces, but side suits and trump distribution still matter.

feedback.title: A cautious Sans plan
feedback.summary: Four Sans has top-card support, but losing trump protection makes your long-suit continuation less secure.
points: Control: the top four Hearts and two side Aces remain useful without trump.
Risk: 7-4-2 of Clubs offers no high-card stopper against a Club attack.
Access: establishing winners does not ensure you regain the lead to cash them.
